text.text: The NEC PC-98 series was a family of Japanese personal computers introduced in 1982. The platform dominated the Japanese computer market and developed a large software library including business applications, visual novels, strategy games, and role-playing games. Its unique hardware architecture and graphics standards resulted in many titles being developed specifically for the system. The PC-98 remained popular through the 1990s before being replaced by IBM-compatible PCs.
